The image is a microscopic view (scale bar: 100 µm) showing branched conidiophores with dense, grape-like clusters of round conidia at their tips. This is the hallmark morphology of *Botrytis cinerea*:

- Branched conidiophore stalks
- Terminal botryose (grape-like) clusters of round, dark conidia
- Multiple branching points each bearing clustered spore heads

This matches the Gray Mold knowledge base description: "spores are light brown-gray on black stalks" and "dense velvety gray-brown spore mass."
